item.title: Inside the Trump administration’s $2 billion push to build the world’s first useful quantum computer
item.description: The White House Quantum Summit brought together dozens of quantum policy officials and industry leaders last month, representing a rare glimmer of bipartisanship as the U.S. hustles to become the first nation to build a fault-tolerant quantum computer.
item.dc:creator: Inc., Fast Company

item.title: Rust preps improved borrow checker for stabilization
item.description: The Rust team has announced that it is enabling the Polonius Alpha borrow checker on nightly releases for testing. The team expects to fully stabilize Polonius Alpha later in the year. The announcement was made in a blog post on August 4.
item.dc:creator: Info World

item.title: How humanitarian organizations are using AI to reach people faster
item.description: Minutes after catastrophic earthquakes struck Venezuela in June, GiveDirectly got an AI-generated snapshot of the disaster from an internal tool.
item.dc:creator: Adele Peters, Fast Company

item.title: Top US hedge funds targeted by major vishing campaign
item.description: BlackFile (now known as Redact) has been busy, raking in more than $10 milllion since the start of the year.
item.dc:creator: Sead Fadilpašić, TechRadar

item.title: How to watch DHL Stormers vs New Zealand for FREE: Live streams and TV channels for Rugby's Greatest Rivalry tour opener
item.description: All the ways to watch DHL Stormers vs New Zealand live streams for free from anywhere in the world as Rugby's Greatest Rivalry begins.

item.title: Great news for cheap OLED TVs and monitors: LG's new '2-stack' tech should cost less to make and be more energy efficient than its recent 'OLED SE' panel
item.description: LG's new 2-stack OLED panel is cheaper to make and delivers better color and viewing angles than current WOLED panels, the firm says
item.dc:creator: Carrie Marshall, TechRadar

item.title: Microsoft releases open-source agent that generates unit tests
item.description: Microsoft has released code-testing-generator, an open-source agent for generating unit tests in any programming language, according to the company. Released July 31, the code-testing-generator agent learns from the user’s repository, then plans, writes, and checks the tests to prove that they work.
item.dc:creator: Info World

item.title: Google’s AI leadership comes apart in a single morning
item.description: Welcome to AI Decoded, Fast Company‘s weekly newsletter that breaks down the most important news in the world of AI. I’m Mark Sullivan, a senior writer at Fast Company, covering emerging tech, AI, and tech policy. Sign up to receive this newsletter every week via email here.
item.dc:creator: Mark Sullivan, Fast Company

item.title: Trump’s Head Start overhaul could deepen the digital divide
item.description: The Trump administration is reportedly planning a major overhaul of Head Start, which could strip back the antipoverty mission of the education program. In the long run, that could deepen the digital divide, ultimately impacting the future workforce and U.S. economy.
item.dc:creator: Chris Morris, Fast Company

item.title: Your blood pressure cuff may expose your health data
item.description: FTC cases reveal major health apps disclosed blood pressure and glucose data to advertising and analytics companies without users realizing it.
item.dc:creator: Fox News

item.title: OpenAI’s ‘Rotten to the core’ defense is its weakest play yet
item.description: Ancient Greek sophist Protagoras famously said, “There are two sides to every question.” But OpenAI’s latest attempt at reality distortion seems determined to narrow this dispute to just one.
item.dc:creator: Computer World

item.title: Meta launches Muse Code for complex software work with persistent AI agents
item.description: Meta has released a beta coding agent designed to handle complex software assignments across large codebases. Available for macOS and Linux, Muse Code uses the company’s new Muse Spark 1.2 model.
item.dc:creator: Info World

item.title: AI deepfakes are already in full force this election season
item.description: For years, we’ve been warned about the deleterious effects of deepfakes on our elections: AI-generated videos that can dupe voters into believing candidates have said or done things they haven’t.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Heilweil, Fast Company

item.title: Arista hits first $3B quarter as AI networking demand continues and supply pressures show signs of improvement
item.description: Arista Networks shared some good news about its earnings and future directions during its second-quarter earnings call this week. For starters, Arista reported its first-ever $3 billion quarter.
item.dc:creator: Network World

item.title: Fuego volcano activity that triggered evacuations in Guatemala is decreasing, but risks remain
item.description: Guatemalan authorities say activity at the Fuego volcano is gradually decreasing after it began two days ago.
item.dc:creator: Sonia Pérez D., Associated Press, KPRC 2

item.title: A trip down shareware lane
item.description: I hope you’ll indulge me this week as I take a break from my usual rantings about agentic coding and meander down memory lane. I learned to code BASIC in the mid-1970s at my progressive junior high school. In math class.
item.dc:creator: Info World

item.title: Data center energy constraints and moratoriums are mounting. Expect to see stalled AI projects
item.description: In mid-July, New York became the first state to impose a state-wide moratorium on new data center construction. “Data center development threatens to hike up utility bills, deplete our natural resources, and create uncertainty for New Yorkers,” wrote Governor Kathy Hochul in her executive order.
item.dc:creator: Network World

item.title: Anthropic’s AI models accidentally hacked three companies
item.description: Anthropic has launched an investigation into what went wrong during a recent test of three models that left a trio of companies accidentally hacked.
item.dc:creator: Computer World

item.title: Apple and the invisible wolf: AI slop drowns real security threats
item.description: Apple has had to introduce a quota on security researcher reports because its systems are being overwhelmed by low-quality warnings generated by AI. It’s a classic illustration of the rule of unintended consequences: a technology meant to help us has become a barrier to getting things done.
item.dc:creator: Computer World

item.title: How AI is killing smartphone apps in China
item.description: Chinese smartphone makers have been followers in the global market, embracing the concepts and paradigms set in the past 20 years by Apple and Google. But AI may be giving the Chinese an opportunity to break away and set their own path forward.
item.dc:creator: Computer World
